Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

learn verb

find out

also find out, be told, discover, determine

classical

Cic. Att. 12.1.2: reliqua quae exspectābam ex tuīs litterīs cognōvī omnia
Verg. G. 2.490: fēlīx quī potuit rērum cognōscere causās

cognōscō, cognōscere, cognōvī, cognitum

verb, third conjugation

find out, learn (of)

With an accusative or an accusative and infinitive, and ex or ab for the source: ex tuīs litterīs cognōvī is a stock phrase of Cicero’s letters. The perfect cognōvī means “I know”.

Other words

  • comperiō, comperīre, comperī, compertum — find out (for certain)

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. And. 211: Prīmum jam dē amōre hoc comperit; Caes. BG 1.22 (Lewis & Short): ut posteā ex captīvīs comperit

    Lewis & Short: “to find out with certainty, to have or gain certain information”.

  • certior fierī — be informed, be told

    also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.11 (Lewis & Short): Caesarem certiōrem faciunt

    Active aliquem certiōrem facere, to let someone know: fac mē certiōrem, “let me know” (Cic. Fam. 8.1.1, Caelius).

Examples

  • reliqua quae exspectābam ex tuīs litterīs cognōvī omnia

    Everything else I was waiting for I learned from your letter.Cic. Att. 12.1.2

  • sed sī tantus amor cāsūs cognōscere nostrōs … incipiam

    But if you so long to learn what befell us … I will begin.Verg. A. 2.10–13

  • fac mē certiōrem

    Let me know.Cic. Fam. 8.1.1 (Caelius)

See also learn, hear, know, information.
